rationale.conceptual: The method uses established DFT algorithms (FP-LAPW, PBE-GGA) and standard derived‐property calculations (Birch-Murnaghan fit, Kramers-Kronig, elastic constants via finite strain, Voigt-Reuss-Hill averaging). It is not a novel method, but correctly implementing this range of physics properties from a single DFT code constitutes a non-trivial, multi-part algorithm that requires careful handling of convergence, unit conversions, and post-processing formulas.
rationale.execution: The pipeline involves five distinct stages (structural optimization across three phases, DOS, optical dielectric function, elastic constants, mechanical/thermal post-processing), each dependent on previous outputs. It requires integration with an external DFT tool (WIEN2k or equivalent), library installation, pseudopotential acquisition, and scripted post-processing. This is a multi-stage workflow with moderate orchestration, though no heavy data acquisition or fragile distributed computing.
